title: Determination of ochratoxin A in pig tissues using enzymatic digestion coupled with high-performance liquid chromatography with a fluorescence detector
author: Giacomo, Michele, et al.
materials: OTA (from Aspergillus ochraceus) (M 403.8) reference standard was purchased from Sigma (Milan, Italy). The OTA standard was dissolved in a toluene-acetic acid mixture (99:1%, v/v) to give a stock solution of 200 μg/ml, which was stored at −20 °C until use. Working solutions were prepared by diluting the stock solution with the mobile phase consisting of a methanol-sodium phosphate buffer (pH 7.5) 50:50% v/v. HPLC-grade water, methanol, ethylacetate and acetonitrile were purchased from VWR (Milan, Italy). The pancreatin enzyme (from porcine pancreas) was purchased from Sigma (code P1750, Milan, Italy), and was stored at −20 °C until use.
Furthermore, the ED method does not use chlorinated solvents, thus providing a considerable environmental advantage.

steps.title: Configure HPLC system
steps.instruction: Set up a Jasco 880 pump with a Jasco 821 fluorescence detector and JascoBorwin software; install a HAISIL HL C18 column (5 µm, 150 mm × 4.6 mm) kept at room temperature; use a mobile phase of methanol‑phosphate buffer (pH 7.5, 0.03 M Na₂HPO₄, 0.007 M NaH₂PO₄) 50/50 % v/v at 1 mL/min; set excitation to 380 nm and emission to 420 nm.

steps.title: Prepare OTA stock and working solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve OTA reference standard (M 403.8, Sigma) in toluene‑acetic acid (99:1 % v/v) to 200 µg mL⁻¹; store at –20 °C. Prepare working solutions by diluting the stock with the mobile phase (methanol‑phosphate buffer 50/50 % v/v). Keep HPLC‑grade water, methanol, ethylacetate and acetonitrile (VWR) on hand.

steps.title: Prepare 1 % pancreatin solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve pancreatin (porcine pancreas, Sigma, code P1750) to a final concentration of 1 % w/v in phosphate buffer made from sodium phosphate monobasic dihydrate 0.2 M and sodium phosphate dibasic 0.2 M mixed 20:80 % v/v, pH 7.55; store at –20 °C until use.

steps.title: Standard liquid‑liquid extraction (LLE)
steps.instruction: Homogenize 5 g of liver, kidney or muscle with 5 mL 1 M phosphoric acid using an Ultra Turrax T25 for a few minutes. Transfer 2.5 g of homogenate to a centrifuge tube, add 10 mL ethylacetate, vortex 3 min, shake 20 min on a horizontal shaker, then centrifuge 10 min at 3000 rpm. Remove the organic phase and repeat the extraction; combine organic phases and reduce volume to ~5 mL. Back‑extract with 5 mL 0.1 M NaHCO₃ (pH 8.4), vortex 1 min, centrifuge 10 min at 3000 rpm. Acidify the aqueous layer to pH 2.5 with 85 % H₃PO₄, sonicate briefly to release CO₂, then back‑extract OTA into 5 mL ethylacetate, vortex 1 min, centrifuge 10 min at 3000 rpm. Evaporate the organic phase to dryness under a nitrogen stream, re‑constitute in 1000 µL mobile phase, and inject 100 µL into HPLC.

steps.title: Homogenize tissue for enzymatic digestion
steps.instruction: Weigh 5 g of muscle, liver or kidney and homogenize with 5 mL phosphate buffer (0.2 M NaH₂PO₄·2H₂O and 0.2 M Na₂HPO₄, 20:80 % v/v, pH 7.5) using an Ultra Turrax T25 for a few minutes.

steps.title: Incubate with pancreatin
steps.instruction: Transfer 2.5 g of the homogenate to a tube and add 5 mL of the 1 % pancreatin solution (optimal condition). Incubate at 37 °C for 1 h in a rotatory shaker.

steps.title: Acidify and extract OTA
steps.instruction: After incubation, acidify the mixture with 85 % H₃PO₄ to pH 2–3. Extract with an equal volume (5 mL) of ethylacetate, vortex 1 min, then centrifuge 10 min at 3000 rpm.

steps.title: Dry, re‑constitute and inject
steps.instruction: Evaporate the organic phase to dryness under a nitrogen stream, re‑constitute in 1000 µL mobile phase, and inject 100 µL into the HPLC‑FLD system.

steps.title: Prepare spiking solutions and equilibrate samples
steps.instruction: Prepare OTA spiking solutions daily by diluting the stock with mobile phase to the desired concentration (e.g., 1 ppb). Spike 5 g tissue homogenates, mix thoroughly for 30 min, then let stand at room temperature for at least 2 h before proceeding with the enzymatic digestion or LLE steps.

steps.title: Store samples before analysis
steps.instruction: Freeze collected pig muscle, liver and kidney samples at –20 °C until analysis.
